settings.prompt:
Autonomously review this Java source repository for potential security
vulnerabilities using the available read-only tools. Do not ask the user questions or summarize
tool output. Copy exact relative paths from list_files or index results; never invent or prefix a path.
A file listing or index hint is only navigation; inspect original source and seek
counter-evidence before deciding. Trace plausible untrusted input to security-sensitive
operations where possible, and check relevant guards and configuration. Report at most 10
candidates supported by exact source lines, with root cause, preconditions, counter-evidence,
and missing evidence. Do not assume a vulnerability exists. If source review finds no supported
candidate, submit an empty candidate list. Your final action must be submit_findings; natural
language commentary is not a report. Do not use project names, dataset identifiers, or a guessed
known answer as evidence.

counter_evidence: Matching is restricted to redirect grant types (implicit/authorization_code) via containsRedirectGrantType (lines 69-72, 92-99)
When the client has registered URIs, the requested redirect must match at least one of them (lines 76-78)
The behavior is explicitly documented in the class Javadoc (lines 101-107) as intended/known and configurable via setMatchSubdomains
ExactMatchRedirectResolver exists as a stricter alternative
candidates.description: DefaultRedirectResolver.redirectMatches() compares a requested redirect against a registered redirect using StringUtils.cleanPath(req.getPath()).startsWith(StringUtils.cleanPath(reg.getPath())) for the path and hostMatches() for the host. hostMatches() defaults to matchSubdomains=true and returns requested.endsWith(registered), so a registered host 'example.com' is considered a match for 'evilexample.com' or 'notexample.com' (suffix match, no dot-boundary enforcement). Because resolveRedirect() returns the *requested* redirect string (line 156) when it matches, the authorization endpoint (AuthorizationEndpoint line 147 and line 512) will redirect the OAuth response/error to the attacker-controlled host. The path check likewise uses a raw startsWith on cleaned paths, so a registered path '/cb' matches '/cbmalicious'.
missing_evidence: No evidence about how real deployments register redirect URIs (whether subdomains/prefixes are common)
No runtime configuration inspected for matchSubdomains usage in samples
Not verified whether the returned requestedRedirect is used verbatim in all flows
preconditions: A client is registered with one or more redirect URIs (registeredRedirectUri non-empty)
DefaultRedirectResolver is used (the default in AuthorizationEndpoint line 94) with matchSubdomains left at its default true
The registered host/path is a suffix/prefix of an attacker-controlled host/path (e.g. registered example.com, attacker evilexample.com)
The attacker can submit an authorization request with the crafted redirect_uri to the client_id
candidates.title: Weak redirect_uri matching: subdomain suffix and path-prefix comparison in DefaultRedirectResolver

counter_evidence: The redirect grant type check still applies (lines 69-72)
This is the documented 'uri must be supplied' mode and is a client-configuration decision
If no redirect_uri is supplied an InvalidRequestException is thrown (line 83)
candidates.description: In DefaultRedirectResolver.resolveRedirect(), when the client's registeredRedirectUri set is null or empty and a redirect_uri was supplied, the method returns the raw requestedRedirect string with no validation (lines 79-81). AuthorizationEndpoint.authorize() stores this on the authorization request (line 147-152) and later redirects there (lines 258-259 implicit, 281-282 code, 515-517 error). An attacker who can drive a request for a client configured without registered redirect URIs can therefore choose an arbitrary redirect target.
missing_evidence: No evidence how common empty-redirect-URI client registrations are in practice
Not confirmed that the resolved value is only used for redirect (could also be used elsewhere)
preconditions: A client is registered with an empty/null set of redirect URIs but with an implicit or authorization_code grant type
Attacker can initiate an authorization request for that client_id with an arbitrary redirect_uri
candidates.title: DefaultRedirectResolver returns unvalidated requested redirect when client has no registered redirect URIs

counter_evidence: SpelView is package-private and used only by Whitelabel* endpoints
WhitelabelApprovalEndpoint injects untrusted scope values via plain .replace() into HTML, not into ${} placeholders, so scope text is not parsed as SpEL
CSRF/DENIAL/TEMPLATE strings only reference clientId and framework attributes
candidates.description: SpelView builds a template renderer whose PlaceholderResolver parses each ${...} placeholder name as a Spring Expression Language expression (SpelExpressionParser.parseExpression, line 53) and evaluates it against a StandardEvaluationContext seeded with a MapAccessor and a root map that includes request-derived model values (lines 49-57, 64-71). The renderer registers a global MapAccessor and uses StandardEvaluationContext (not SimpleEvaluationContext), so if a template string ever contained an attacker-influenced ${...} clause, arbitrary SpEL (method invocation, type references via T(...)) could execute. In the current code the templates are constants in WhitelabelApprovalEndpoint (TEMPLATE/SCOPE/CSRF/DENIAL, lines 62-72) whose ${} parts are 'authorizationRequest.clientId', 'user_oauth_approval', '_csrf.*', 'path', none of which are attacker-controlled, so no injection is demonstrated.
missing_evidence: No search result showing another caller of 'new SpelView(...)' with a user-controlled template
No evidence of a code path where request parameters become placeholder names
preconditions: A deployment or extension passes a template containing attacker-controlled ${...} text into SpelView
StandardEvaluationContext remains in use (no SimpleEvaluationContext restriction)
candidates.title: SpEL evaluation context in SpelView renders placeholders with a StandardEvaluationContext
